current_example.title: Example: Finding a Function's Root Using the Newton-Raphson Method

q-256514.name: Question 1
q-256514.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=(\operatorname{sin}⁡((x-4)^{2})-(x-6))^{′}=2(x-4)\operatorname{cos}⁡((x-4)^{2})-1
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(({x}_{n}-4)^{2})-({x}_{n}-6)}{2({x}_{n}-4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(({x}_{n}-4)^{2})-1} \\ .\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=5.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(({x}_{0}-4)^{2})-({x}_{0}-6)}{2({x}_{0}-4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(({x}_{0}-4)^{2})-1} \\  & =5.5-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2.25)+0.5}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(2.25)-1} \\  & ≈5.943,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

q-256514.html:
Question 1
?
Suppose we wish to find a root of the function f(x)=sin⁡((x−4)2)−(x−6) in the interval [5,6]. Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting from the point x0=5.5. Round your answer to three decimal places.
x1≈
5.943
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

xn+1=xn−f(xn)f′(xn)

where f′(xn) is the derivative of f(x) evaluated at xn.

In our case, we have

f′(x)=(sin⁡((x−4)2)−(x−6))′=2(x−4)cos⁡((x−4)2)−1

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

xn+1=xn−sin⁡((xn−4)2)−(xn−6)2(xn−4)cos⁡((xn−4)2)−1.

Starting with x0=5.5, we have

x1=x0−sin⁡((x0−4)2)−(x0−6)2(x0−4)cos⁡((x0−4)2)−1=5.5−sin⁡(2.25)+0.53cos⁡(2.25)−1≈5.943, rounded to three decimal places.

q-256513.name: Question 3
q-256513.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\frac{x-4}{5})}^{′}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{1}{5}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}-4}{5}}{-\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{n}-\frac{1}{5}} \\  & ={x}_{n}+\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{n}-{x}_{n}+4}{5\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{n}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=4.8,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{0}-{x}_{0}+4}{5\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{0}+1} \\  & =4.8+\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4.8)-4.8+4}{5\operatorname{sin}⁡(4.8)+1} \\  & ≈4.891,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

q-255771.name: Question 6
q-255771.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({x}^{3}-x-1)^{′}=3{x}^{2}-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{3}-{x}_{n}-1}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(3{x}_{n}^{2}-1)-({x}_{n}^{3}-{x}_{n}-1)}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2{x}_{n}^{3}+1}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{2{x}_{0}^{3}+1}{3{x}_{0}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1)^{3}+1}{3(1)^{2}-1} \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{2{x}_{1}^{3}+1}{3{x}_{1}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1.5)^{3}+1}{3(1.5)^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{7.75}{5.75} \\  & ≈1.348,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

q-255772.name: Question 10
q-255772.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)^{′}=\frac{1}{x}.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-1}{(\frac{1}{{x}_{n}})} \\  & ={x}_{n}-({x}_{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-{x}_{n}) \\  & =2{x}_{n}-{x}_{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =2{x}_{0}-{x}_{0}\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{0} \\  & =2(1.5)-(1.5)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(1.5) \\  & =2.391\,802….\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =2{x}_{1}-{x}_{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{1} \\  & =2(2.391\,802…)-(2.391\,802…)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(2.391\,802…) \\  & =2.697\,840….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}≈2.392$ and ${x}_{2}≈2.698,$ rounded to three decimal places.

q-256612.name: Question 11
q-256612.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({x}^{4}-8x-3)^{′}=4{x}^{3}-8.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{4}-8{x}_{n}-3}{4{x}_{n}^{3}-8} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(4{x}_{n}^{3}-8)-({x}_{n}^{4}-8{x}_{n}-3)}{4{x}_{n}^{3}-8} \\  & =\frac{3({x}_{n}^{4}+1)}{4({x}_{n}^{3}-2)}.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{3({x}_{0}^{4}+1)}{4({x}_{0}^{3}-2)} \\  & =\frac{3({2}^{4}+1)}{4({2}^{3}-2)} \\  & =\frac{51}{24} \\  & =2.125.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{3({x}_{1}^{4}+1)}{4({x}_{1}^{3}-2)} \\  & =\frac{3((2.125)^{4}+1)}{4((2.125)^{3}-2)} \\  & =2.112…, \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{3({x}_{2}^{4}+1)}{4({x}_{2}^{3}-2)} \\  & =\frac{3((2.112…)^{4}+1)}{4((2.112…)^{3}-2)} \\  & =2.111….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations ${x}_{2}≈2.11$ and ${x}_{3}≈2.11$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the root of the function is $x≈2.11,$ rounded to two decimal places.

q-256604.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({x}^{3}-x-4)^{′}=3{x}^{2}-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{3}-x-4}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(3{x}_{n}^{2}-1)-({x}_{n}^{3}-{x}_{n}-4)}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2{x}_{n}^{3}+4}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{2{x}_{0}^{3}+4}{3{x}_{0}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1.5)^{3}+4}{3(1.5)^{2}-1} \\  & =1.869…\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{2{x}_{1}^{3}+4}{3{x}_{1}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1.869…)^{3}+4}{3(1.869…)^{2}-1} \\  & =1.799…, \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{2{x}_{2}^{3}+4}{3{x}_{2}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1.799…)^{3}+4}{3(1.799…)^{2}-1} \\  & =1.796….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations ${x}_{2}≈1.8$ and ${x}_{3}≈1.8$ are the same when rounded to one decimal place.

Therefore, the root of the function is $x≈1.8,$ rounded to one decimal place.
